name: The Gates of Hell
kicker: Auguste Rodin’s unfinished bronze doorway · Scenes from Dante’s _Inferno_
briefing: French sculptor Auguste Rodin spent 37 years working on a single pair of bronze doors and never considered them finished. Commissioned for a museum that was never built, the doors crowd more than 180 wrestling, falling figures drawn from Dante’s _Inferno_ onto one six-meter-tall frame. Rodin kept enlarging his favorite figures into famous statues of their own, including the brooding man now known as _The Thinker_ — itself a separate answer line, so don’t mix them up.
answerHtml: The Gates of Hell (or La Porte de l’Enfer)

tossups.p: Rodin planned large figures of Adam and Eve to flank this work, but he left his Eve unfinished after realizing his model was pregnant. An early relief panel for this work titled _Francesca da Rimini_ was scrapped and replaced for not showing enough suffering.
tossups.r: That rejected embrace of the doomed lovers later became famous on its own as _The Kiss_. For 10 points, name this sculptural doorway by Auguste Rodin, based on Dante’s _Inferno_.

tossups.p: A _Fallen Caryatid_ figure built for this work was later given an added stone to carry on her back. Plaster studies tracing this work’s long development are preserved today at the Musée Rodin’s casting site in Meudon, France.
tossups.r: Its sculptor worked from Dante studies alone for about a year before restarting the project using live models. For 10 points, name this unfinished bronze doorway crowded with figures from the _Inferno_, by Auguste Rodin.

tossups.p: This work was modeled partly on Lorenzo Ghiberti’s earlier bronze doors for the Baptistery of Florence. A figure called _Meditation_ on this work shows a woman resting her head on her bent arm, and a separate figure known as _I Am Beautiful_ pairs a Crouching Woman with a Falling Man.
tossups.r: Over 180 figures crowd this doorway, ranging from a few centimeters to more than a meter tall. For 10 points, name this bronze sculptural group depicting scenes from Dante’s _Inferno_, created by Auguste Rodin.

tossups.p: Bronze casts of this work made after its sculptor’s death now stand in Paris, Philadelphia, and Tokyo, among other cities. Its sculptor drew inspiration not just from Dante but also from Michelangelo’s _The Last Judgment_ and the poetry of Charles Baudelaire [“bohd-LAIR”].
tossups.r: The original full-size plaster model is kept today at the Musée d’Orsay in Paris. For 10 points, name this bronze doorway crowded with suffering figures, sculpted by Auguste Rodin.

tossups.p: This work’s sculptor was commissioned in 1880 to design it for the entrance of a planned Decorative Arts Museum that was never built. At the very top of this work, three identical figures with joined, pointing hands look down at the suffering below.
tossups.r: Its sculptor, Auguste Rodin, kept revising it for the rest of his life and never finished it in bronze before dying in 1917. For 10 points, name this unfinished doorway based on Dante’s _Inferno_.

tossups.p: One figure built for this work shows Count Ugolino on his knees over his dying sons, a tragic scene of starvation from Dante’s poem. Overall, this bronze doorway measures about six meters tall, four meters wide, and a meter deep.
tossups.r: A brooding, bare man resting his chin on his hand sits above the doors of this work; that figure was later enlarged into its own famous statue. For 10 points, name this sculptural group by Auguste Rodin, inspired by Dante’s _Inferno_.

tossups.p: This work includes a grieving father crouched over his starving children, based on the story of Count Ugolino. A pair of doomed lovers named Paolo and Francesca, first modeled embracing for this work, was later removed and enlarged into its own statue.
tossups.r: Rodin never considered this bronze doorway finished, even though he worked on it for 37 years. For 10 points, name this sculptural group inspired by Dante’s _Inferno_, which also contains the statue later known as _The Thinker_.

tossups.p: This work’s sculptor originally modeled its brooding central figure, now famous on its own, as a small-scale representation of the poet Dante looking down at the suffering below him. Paolo and Francesca da Rimini appear within this work, though an earlier, happier version of the pair was removed and cast separately as _The Kiss_.
tossups.r: Over 180 figures of various sizes crowd this unfinished bronze doorway. For 10 points, name this sculptural group by Auguste Rodin, inspired by Dante Alighieri’s _Inferno_.

tossups.p: A scrapped group for this work showing Francesca da Rimini with her lover was removed for seeming too happy for a work about suffering. This work’s sculptor researched Dante’s poem for roughly a year before switching to working from live models.
tossups.r: The finished doorway was cast in bronze only after its sculptor’s death in 1917. For 10 points, name this sculptural group of doors crowded with sinners from Dante’s _Inferno_, created by Auguste Rodin.

tossups.p: Two of this work’s figures, a Crouching Woman and a Falling Man, were combined into a separate group called _I Am Beautiful_, inspired by a line from Charles Baudelaire. This work’s sculptor also separately cast a grieving woman resting her head on her bent arm, titled _Meditation_.
tossups.r: It was commissioned for a museum of decorative arts that was never actually constructed. For 10 points, name this bronze doorway crowded with figures from Dante’s _Inferno_, sculpted by Auguste Rodin.

tossups.p: This work’s sculptor left a planned Eve figure for it unfinished after realizing his model was pregnant. Three identical figures with joined hands, called _The Three Shades_, crown the very top of this doorway, pointing down at the scene below.
tossups.r: No bronze cast of this piece was completed until after its sculptor’s 1917 death. For 10 points, name this sculptural group of doors by Auguste Rodin, based on Dante’s _Inferno_.

tossups.p: This unfinished work was partly modeled on an earlier set of bronze doors by Lorenzo Ghiberti for a Baptistery in Florence. One scene within it shows Count Ugolino trapped in a tower with his starving sons, a story drawn from Dante’s _Inferno_.
tossups.r: More than 180 figures crowd this six-meter-tall doorway. For 10 points, name this bronze sculptural group by Auguste Rodin, whose figures include the statue later known as _The Thinker_.

tossups.p: This sculpture’s original full-size plaster model is now housed at the Musée d’Orsay, while posthumous bronze casts of it stand in cities from Paris to Tokyo. Its sculptor spent 37 years revising it without ever declaring it complete.
tossups.r: It was commissioned in 1880 for a planned museum of decorative arts in Paris. For 10 points, name this unfinished bronze doorway inspired by Dante’s _Inferno_, created by Auguste Rodin.

tossups.p: A pair of doomed lovers, Paolo and Francesca, first modeled for this work, were later enlarged into the statue _The Kiss_, while a grieving father crouched over his starving sons became a separate Ugolino sculpture. This work’s many figures range in height from a few centimeters to over a meter.

Three figures with joined hands crown its top, and a brooding man above its panels was later enlarged into his own famous statue.
tossups.r: Rodin worked on this bronze doorway for the rest of his life after an 1880 commission for a museum that was never built. For 10 points, name this sculptural group inspired by Dante’s _Inferno_.

A brooding, bare man resting his chin on his hand, perched above the doors, was later enlarged into the famous statue _The Thinker_ — its own separate answer line, so don’t confuse the two
Depicts a mass of suffering souls meant to loom over visitors walking through an actual set of entrance doors
Commissioned in 1880 for the entrance of a planned Decorative Arts Museum in Paris that was never built
Rodin kept revising it for the rest of his life and never finished it in bronze; he died in 1917
The original full-size plaster model is kept today at the Musée d’Orsay in Paris
The doomed lovers Paolo and Francesca, first modeled embracing for this work, were removed and enlarged into the separate statue _The Kiss_
Shows Count Ugolino on his knees over his dying sons, a tragic scene of starvation from Dante’s poem
Three identical figures with joined, pointing hands, called _The Three Shades_, crown the very top of the doors
Two of its figures, Crouching Woman and Falling Man, were combined into a separate group called _I Am Beautiful_, inspired by Charles Baudelaire’s poetry
Partly modeled on Lorenzo Ghiberti’s earlier bronze doors for the Baptistery of Florence, nicknamed the Gates of Paradise
Rodin planned figures of Adam and Eve to flank the doors, but left Eve unfinished after realizing his model was pregnant
An early relief panel titled _Francesca da Rimini_ was scrapped and replaced for not showing enough suffering
A _Fallen Caryatid_ figure on the doors was later given an added stone to carry on her back
A figure called _Meditation_ shows a grieving woman resting her head on her bent arm
Bronze casts made after Rodin’s death stand today in Paris, Philadelphia, and Tokyo, among other cities
The bronze doorway stands about six meters (nearly 20 feet) tall, four meters wide, and a meter deep
More than 180 individual figures, from a few centimeters to over a meter tall, crowd the doors

Besides Dante, Rodin also drew on Michelangelo’s _The Last Judgment_ and the poetry of Charles Baudelaire

trap.title: Doorway or The Thinker?
trap.body: _The Gates of Hell_ contains dozens of embedded figures, including _The Thinker_, _The Three Shades_, and _Ugolino and His Sons_; even _The Kiss_ began as part of it. Several real tossups whose actual answer is “_The Thinker_” prompt on “_The Gates of Hell_” because their early clues — a museum commission, an assistant who enlarged it, its original title _The Poet_ — describe only the smaller statue, not the whole bronze doorway.
trap.fix: If every clue describes just ONE single brooding man resting his chin on his hand, the safer buzz is _The Thinker_, not the whole doorway. Only answer _The Gates of Hell_ once the clues mention SEVERAL different embedded sculptures together — _The Three Shades_, Ugolino, Paolo and Francesca — as pieces of one giant set of doors.
trap.line: Real answer line: The Gates of Hell [or La Porte de l’Enfer].
